newsitem.title: USA: CLECO rate pact limits return on equity.
newsitem.headline: CLECO rate pact limits return on equity.

text.p: Central Louisiana Electric Co Inc said Thursday the rate agreement approved by the Louisiana Public Service Commission limits the utility's return on equity.
This plan will allow CLECO to retain all earnings equating to a return on equity up to and including 12.25 percent on its regulated utility operations, the company said.

Any earnings over 12.25 percent, up to and including 13 percent, will be shared equally between CLECO and its customers, which effectively provides CLECO with the opportunity to realize a rate of return of up to 12.625.
The utility earned a rate of return of 12.5 percent in 1995, Secretary-Treasurer Michael Prudhomme said.
Any earnings above a 13 percent return on equity would be refunded fully to customers, CLECO said.

As announced Wednesday, the settlement calls for a $3 million reduction to CLECO's annual base rate tariff effective November 1, 1996, and an additional reduction of $2 million effective January 1, 1998.
During the five-year period beginning November 1, a rate stabilization plan will be in place, the company noted.

During the five-year period, it said, CLECO will have the right to apply for a rate increase if a significant event affecting its earnings would justify it, such as regulatory or economic changes, major hurricane damage, or other unforeseen circumstances.

During the period, the company will also be able to propose for commission consideration any revenue-neutral rate design changes it feels appropriate, such as revenue redistribution among customer classes which may be warranted.
Also, during the period, the commission may amend or modify any of the settlement's terms should it determine changes are warranted by the public interest.

Based on the earnings review's test year, which was the 12 months ending March 1995, the $3 million reduction on November 1 is the equivalent of a decrease in annual base revenues of about 1.2 percent, and the $2 million reduction scheduled for January 1, 1998, will reduce annual base revenues by about 0.8 percent, for a total reduction in annual base revenues of approximately two percent over the 14-month period, CLECO said.
